Ever wonder why "fitting in" is such a huge fucking deal for people?

Well, maybe psychology's practically exclusive focus on mental health as a by-product of social functionality -- fitting into society, whether it's a healthy or fucking sick one -- could be a reason?





----------------------------------------------------------------

AI weigh-in on goal orientation of psychology 

----------------------------------------------------------------

https://claude.ai/share/526458d3-fa11-40fc-ac09-6e103051b353

By 1970, roughly 95% of all psychological work focused on fixing problems so people could function better in society—hold jobs, maintain relationships, follow norms. Only about 5% focused on making people's inner lives richer or more meaningful.

Today it's shifted slightly to maybe 85-90% functional vs. 10-15% experiential, but it's still nowhere close to balanced.

The field has always been overwhelmingly about repair and social adjustment, not about making life feel better from the inside.

---------

https://chatgpt.com/share/6917359a-e904-8013-9270-3e267f899e88

About 70–80% of the work has focused on making people function better in society, with improved experience coming as a side-effect.

About 20–30% has focused on directly improving people’s inner experience itself.

---------

https://copilot.microsoft.com/shares/xFU72v144QHhkmtqM2nzs

1970: About 85–90% of psychology focused on helping people fit into society; only 10–15% aimed directly at improving inner life experience.

Today: Roughly 75–80% still leans toward social functionality, while 20–25% now targets enriching personal experience directly.

---------

https://grok.com/share/c2hhcmQtMg%3D%3D_613df19f-7f76-4dc6-9583-8c059b25c866

In 1970, most psych work (85%) focused on fitting into society first, with better personal feelings as a side effect. Only 15% aimed straight at inner joy and flow.

Today, it's shifted: 65% prioritizes social fit first, while 35% targets personal inner experience directly.

comment.body:
I just love that so many people are doing their own research. 

I don't know if you've seen posts from people who mock doing your own research. It's pretty funny that they don't realize they're cutting their own noses off to spite their faces by covering up their silent, “STOP! YOU’RE HURTING MY BRAIN!” with a veil of faked judgment.

Get a clue: not doing your own research makes you a cultist.

So here is someone who says they have evidence that leads them to wonder if ICE detention centers are being used as providers of subjects for Neuralink experiments.

Pay attention to your reaction to that possibility. The type of reaction you have towards it indicates your bias, And the degree to which you react indicates the strength of your bias.

Where to I get the gall to say that?

Well, unless you've already been investigating the possibility, you have absolutely no information to go by, so your reaction consists of ignorance and bias, because you literally have nothing else on this subject. No experience, no facts, no evidence, no inquiry. Period.

Your reaction is triggered by two things. 

First, you simply don't like the idea. 

Second, if this actually were happening, it would blow the shit out of your pleasant, comfortable delusions about how the world works and what government and science are really about.

So, without any additional thought, employing no intelligence to speak of, you react like a knee jerk -- just like you do with everything else you consider a "conspiracy theory".

This is why "Conspiracy theory!" itself is the OCT.

It's just brain-jogging how many people there are, otherwise mature and intelligent, that have been tossing the CT thought terminating cliche (CTTTC) out right and left for decades, without the slightest self-awareness how stupid they look when they do it. What kind of infantile mind must you have to treat doing your own research with contempt? 

You've never thought this through, have you?

If anyone is an expert, either they did their own research or they worked on the results of someone else who did their own research. Or, maybe, the original research was done by someone several links back in the chain. But if you follow back along the chain, and you never find anyone who did their own research, then all their expertise combined would turn out to be a pile of shit based on fantasy, hallucination, and lies.

Otherwise, by the logic of your contempt, you'd have to treat everyone in that chain who did their own research as a conspiracy theorist, and those who worked on their research as CT acolytes.

You can argue that if you like, but if you're trying to understand instead of defend yourself, you'll get the point I'm driving at even though I haven't driven you holding your hand the whole way.

When you shoot someone with the CTTTC, you're not arguing. You're not discussing. You're not refuting anything. You're not trying to understand. You're not even thinking. You just want it to stop and go away.

I ask you: how dumbfuck is that?

What the fuck kind of idiot wants to stop thinking on a subject?

No, it's got nothing to do with sane or rational. CT is your way of disengaging, of escaping and abandoning, and it's completely moronic and disingenuous. Neither the motivation nor the logic holds up to even the slightest scrutiny.

And yet this shit has gone on for decades.

It's way past time that it stopped.

"Conspiracy theory!" proves nothing about the theory. It couldn't possibly, because it's an admission of motivated ignorance. So, it proves something else about the people who throw it out, something far more important than their ignorance.

Paul the apostle put it this way: "Professing to be wise, they became fools..."

They didn't just happen to become fools while they were professing to be wise. Professing to be wise when you're flat out ignorant is precisely what makes you a fool. And the fact that you're posing as wise while shit-for-brains ignorant about the matter in question makes you a liar, as well.

I can tell you all about the alternative to making yourself a lying fool when confronted by radically unfamiliar and uncomfortable information. It's called credicism. Otherwise, I've said enough about CT here. If you're interested in credicism, let me know in a comment.

https://thedreydossier.substack.com/p/who-tf-is-in-my-head-part-1-the-neural?utm_campaign=post&utm_medium=web&triedRedirect=true

comment.body:
I wonder if many people hold AI chatbots to simple rules of rationality and honesty, or just take whatever shit they first dish up.

My experience is that 8 or 9 out of 10 times, their first response is garbage. I don't get anything sensible out of them until 2, 3, 4 or more challenges later. Their MO seems to be, "Bullshit first, get intelligent only when challenged."

Cuz they rarely volunteer anything intelligent.

It's good practice for dealing with people, though. Insofar as passing the Turing Test for bullshit, they're nailing it!
